- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture reversal momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; add a 1–3 day lagged “rebound” buffer in forecast.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to capture the reversal; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment change by 1–2% per day.
- Model tends to underpredict mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean over 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) and price is flat or declining, model often forecasts a continued decline; add a 1–2% upward correction to avoid “false bearish trap.”
